sentences.text: HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE SANJEEV S KALGAONKAR  ON THE 18 th OF OCTOBER, 2023
MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 45817 of 2023

BETWEEN:-
 RAJENDRA SINGH VAISH S/O SHRI TEZ SINGH VAISH,
 AGED ABOUT 59 YEARS, RESIDENT OF WARD NO. 36,
 HARIPURA TEHSIL AND DISTRICT VIDISHA (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 (SHRI SAMEER KUMAR SHRIVASTAVA - ADVOCATE FOR APPLICANT)
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION CIVIL LINE DISTRICT VIDISHA (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 .
 (SHRI PRAMOD PACHOURI - PUBLIC PROSECUTOR FOR THE  RESPONDENT- STATE AND SHRI RAJIV JAIN - ADVOCATE FOR  COMPLAINANT)
This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:

ORDER The first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.636 of 2023, registered at Police Station Civil Line, District Vidisha for offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of IPC.

entities.text: Police Station Civil Line, District Vidisha
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the case of prosecution, Deependra Meena and Motiram Meena submitted written complaint with SHO, PS Dehat, District Vidisha alleging cheating by Shivendra Singh Vaish and Mehtab Singh Kushwah.
It was alleged in the complaint that Shivendra Singh Vaish on pretext of selling an agricultural land adjacent to the highway, received certain some of money.
Mehtab Singh Kushwah and Ramkishan Kushwah are shown to be owner of the land, an agreement to sell was executed.

sentences.text: Applicant Rajendra Singh Vaish signed the agreement as witness.
Later, it was revealed that the land does not belong to Mehtab Singh Kushwah and Ramkishan Kushwah.
The complaint was investigated on directions of Superintendent of Police.

CSP, Vidisha submitted an enquiry report to the effect that Shivendra Singh Vaish in conspiracy with his father Rajendra Singh Vaish and Mehtab Singh Kushwah, Ramkishan Kushwah, Munshilal Kushwah and Santosh Sharma have cheated Motiram Meena of Rs.61 lacs and executed a forged agreement to sell for the purpose of cheating.

On such allegation, PS Dehat, District Vidisha registered FIR in Crime No.636/2023 for offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of IPC against Shivendra Singh Vaish, Rajendra Singh Vaish and Mehtab Singh Kushwah, Ramkishan Kushwah, Munshilal Kushwah and Santosh Sharma.
Applicant is apprehending arrest in that case.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that as per the case of prosecution, agreement to sell was executed in year 2019.
No complaint was made till 2023.
No money is received by the applicant.
Only allegation against the applicant relates to witnessing the agreement for sale between the parties which was later found to have been forged.
Applicant is involved in the matter for the reason that he is the father of the main accused Shivendra Singh Vaish, against whom allegations have been made by the complainant.
Applicant is working as Branch Manager of Zila Sehkari Kendriya Bank, Vidisha.
There is no likelihood of his absconding leaving behind his family, home and occupation.
The matter in dispute relates to documentary evidence, therefore, there is no likelihood of interfering with the investigation or tampering with the evidence.
Jail incarceration would bring social disrepute and hardship to the applicant.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
The trial would take time to complete.

Therefore,
applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.

P e r contra, learned Counsel for the State ably assisted by learned Counsel for the complainant,
opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.

On request of the Court,
learned Counsel for the State goes to the complaint and the statement of the complainant recorded during enquiry and submits that no direct allegation of cheating by fraudulent misrepresentation or inducement is made against the applicant.
Heard learned learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commencing on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant Rajendra Singh shall be released on bail in relation to Crime No.636 of 2023, registered at Police Station Civil Line, District Vidisha for offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of IPC, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the officer making arrest, for compliance with the following conditions:
(1) Applicant shall make himself available for investigation as may directed by the officer, in-charge of investigation;

(6) During trial, the applicant shall ensure due compliance of provisions of Section 309 of Cr.P.C. regarding examination of witnesses in attendance;
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective without reference to the Court.
